classifications.summary: Bergland or Kindelan scale on occlusal radiograph (type I bone to normal height to type IV no bony bridge), and CBCT volumetric fill percentage; a 2024 series defined a critical-size cleft volume of about 810 mm3 for iliac crest and 885 mm3 for rhBMP-2 plus DBM beyond which both fail more often.

why_biologic: To avoid the iliac crest donor site in a child; rhBMP-2 on collagen sponge (off-label, patients under 18 are excluded from the Infuse label), DBM alone or as a carrier, and bone marrow aspirate concentrate are used. Pooled RCT and cohort data show bone fill roughly equal to iliac crest with shorter operations and stays, more facial swelling, and low-certainty evidence; graft failure rises sharply above the critical-size cleft volume for both materials.
autograft_standard: Iliac crest cancellous bone graft in the mixed dentition is the standard of care; donor site pain in up to 87.5 percent in one RCT, gait disturbance, longer stay. Mandibular symphysis, calvarium and rib are alternatives with less bone (symphysis performs at least as well, calvarium and rib worse in the 2017 best-evidence synthesis).
volume_note: CDC National Birth Defects Prevention Network 2010 to 2014: cleft lip with or without cleft palate 10.00 per 10,000 live births (about 1 in 1,000, often quoted as 1 in 1,050 by NIDCR) and cleft palate alone about 1 in 1,600; the 2016 to 2020 update reports a decreasing prevalence of cleft lip with or without palate (PMID 38277408). ACPA quotes 6,000 to 8,000 US children born each year with a cleft; roughly 60 to 75 percent of complete clefts involve the alveolus and reach secondary grafting age.

name: Maxillary sinus floor augmentation and localized alveolar ridge augmentation (extraction socket defects) for dental implants

classifications.name: Residual bone height
classifications.summary: Lateral-window (two-stage) sinus lift when residual posterior maxillary bone is under about 5 to 6 mm; transcrestal (osteotome) lift when 5 to 8 mm remains; the Infuse pivotal trial enrolled patients with under 6 mm.

classifications.name: Extraction socket defect (buccal wall)
classifications.summary: Intact four-wall socket versus buccal wall dehiscence of 50 percent or more; the Infuse ridge indication covers localized augmentation of defects associated with extraction sockets, not vertical or lateral ridge augmentation of the edentulous ridge.

classifications.name: Cawood and Howell ridge atrophy classes I to VI
classifications.summary: From dentate (I) through immediate post-extraction (II), rounded well-formed (III), knife-edge (IV), flat (V) and depressed basal bone (VI); vertical and lateral augmentation of class IV to VI ridges with rhBMP-2 is off-label and usually needs a titanium mesh containment.

why_biologic: This is the one craniomaxillofacial application where a growth factor is on-label: Infuse (rhBMP-2 on absorbable collagen sponge) was approved by PMA P050053 on 2007-03-09 as an alternative to autogenous bone for sinus augmentation and for localized alveolar ridge augmentation for defects associated with extraction sockets, on a 160-patient pivotal RCT. Most sinus lifts are nevertheless done with xenograft (Bio-Oss), allograft (including cellular allografts such as Osteocel Plus) or synthetic particulate because they are cheaper and the Infuse height gain was lower than autograft; adding rhBMP-2 to Bio-Oss reduced new bone in one RCT.
autograft_standard: Intraoral autograft (ramus, symphysis, tuberosity) or iliac crest for large sinus and ridge augmentations; the pivotal trial recorded 17 percent long-term paresthesia, pain or gait disturbance at the autograft donor site.
volume_note: No public US annual count of sinus lifts; dental procedures are not captured by NIS or NEDS. CDT D7951 (lateral sinus augmentation), D7952 (vertical), D7953 (bone replacement graft) are dental codes and the procedure is often excluded or partially covered by dental plans, so volume is private-pay driven.

name: Periodontal intrabony and furcation defect regeneration (adjacent dental application)

classifications.name: Intrabony defect walls
classifications.summary: One-, two- and three-wall intrabony defects of 4 mm or more; Glickman furcation grades I to IV; gingival recession associated with periodontal defects. These are the labeled GEM 21S indications.

why_biologic: Included because GEM 21S (rhPDGF-BB with beta-TCP) is the second CMF growth-factor PMA (P040013, 2005) and the only rhPDGF product in the mouth; the 180-patient pivotal RCT showed faster attachment gain and more bone fill at six months. Enamel matrix derivative (Emdogain), bone allograft and barrier membranes are the competing regenerative approaches.
autograft_standard: Open flap debridement with or without autogenous intraoral bone; the comparison in the pivotal trial was beta-TCP alone.
volume_note: No public US annual count; periodontal regenerative surgery is coded under CDT D4263 and D4265 and is not in hospital datasets.

name: Mandible fracture

classifications.name: Anatomic site
classifications.summary: Symphysis and parasymphysis, body, angle, ramus, condyle and subcondylar, coronoid, dentoalveolar; body, condyle, angle and symphysis make up about two thirds of fractures in the US NTDB.

classifications.name: Favorable versus unfavorable, and load-sharing versus load-bearing
classifications.summary: Fracture line orientation relative to muscle pull; simple fractures are treated with load-sharing miniplates (Champy) or closed reduction with maxillomandibular fixation, while comminuted, atrophic-edentulous, defect and infected fractures need load-bearing reconstruction plates.

classifications.name: Mechanism (US NTDB)
classifications.summary: Assault 37 to 42 percent, motor vehicle crash 22 to 31 percent, falls 15 to 20 percent and rising in elderly women; 78 to 80 percent male.

why_biologic: Standard mandible fractures need no graft. Bone graft is used for comminuted gunshot fractures, atrophic edentulous fractures, infected nonunion and segmental loss, and the graft is autologous (iliac crest, tibia) under a load-bearing plate. rhBMP-2 has been used off-label in defect fractures and nonunion with mixed results (2 of 4 continuity-defect cases failed in the only US series) and no controlled data. Stem cell adjuncts to ORIF are investigational outside the US (NCT02755922, NCT07671183).
autograft_standard: Iliac crest cancellous or corticocancellous block, or proximal tibia, under a reconstruction plate; for large or irradiated defects, the fibula free flap.
volume_note: Nationwide Emergency Department Sample 2018: 28,357 ED encounters with mandibular fracture as the primary diagnosis, 10.2 percent transferred (PMID 36055371); 27,238 weighted isolated mandible fracture encounters, 20 percent admitted (PMID 38403271). NTDB captured 13,142 patients in 2001 to 2005 and 20,391 in 2017 (PMID 26006752, PMID 37291803). Nonunion accounts for 3.6 percent of NIS mandible fracture admissions (PMID 31261344).
hardware_note: Mandible plating systems: Stryker, DePuy Synthes MatrixMANDIBLE (preformed reconstruction plates, 71-patient series PMID 22868032), KLS Martin, Zimmer Biomet, OsteoMed/Acumed; patient-specific selective-laser-melted plates (PMID 40550483).

name: Mandibular continuity (segmental) defect reconstruction

classifications.name: Jewer / HCL (Boyd) classification
classifications.summary: Defects described by segment: C (central, canine to canine), L (lateral, excluding the condyle), H (hemimandible including the condyle), with combinations such as LC, LCL, HC, HCL; modifiers for soft tissue (s, m, o) in the Boyd extension.

classifications.name: Brown classification (2016)
classifications.summary: Class I lateral not crossing the midline, class II hemimandibulectomy including the condyle, class III anterior crossing the midline, class IV extensive anterior and bilateral; with c for condyle.

classifications.name: Etiology
classifications.summary: Oral cancer and benign tumors (ameloblastoma), osteoradionecrosis, medication-related osteonecrosis, osteomyelitis, gunshot and other trauma.

why_biologic: The fibula free flap is the standard and biologics cannot replace a vascularized flap in irradiated or soft-tissue-deficient beds. rhBMP-2 on collagen sponge under a reconstruction plate, with or without a compression-resistant matrix, is used off-label for benign and non-irradiated defects (Herford and Boyne 14-patient series with regeneration in all; Carter 5-patient series with 2 of 4 continuity defects failing); a 2019 safety review graded the evidence as failing to support rhBMP-2 for mandibular reconstruction. Tissue-engineered constructs (EpiBone EB-CMF, axially vascularized ceramics, 3D-printed scaffolds) are first-in-human or preclinical.
autograft_standard: Fibula osteocutaneous free flap with virtual surgical planning; iliac crest free flap and scapula are alternatives with similar failure and complication rates (meta-analysis of 942 patients). Nonvascularized iliac crest block is used for defects under about 6 cm in non-irradiated beds. Donor morbidity is the leg or hip.
volume_note: No public US annual count found for segmental mandibulectomy or mandibular reconstruction (PubMed searched 2026-10-22). Free flap series for osteoradionecrosis pooled 424 flaps across 19 studies (PMID 39580338).
hardware_note: Load-bearing reconstruction plates and patient-specific plates and cutting guides (DePuy Synthes TRUMATCH, Stryker, KLS Martin, Zimmer Biomet); porous polyethylene or titanium mesh containment for rhBMP-2 (30 percent exposure in one 10-defect series, PMID 22209107).

name: Orbital floor and wall fracture reconstruction

classifications.name: Orbital fracture pattern
classifications.summary: Pure blowout (floor, medial wall, combined floor and medial wall), impure blowout with rim involvement, trapdoor fracture in children with muscle entrapment, orbital roof fracture, and orbital fractures as part of zygomaticomaxillary complex or naso-orbito-ethmoid fractures. Surgical indications are enophthalmos over 2 mm, persistent diplopia, entrapment, or a defect larger than about 50 percent of the floor or 2 cm2.

why_biologic: Almost none. Orbital floor reconstruction is an implant market: titanium mesh and preformed orbital plates, porous polyethylene (Medpor) and polyethylene-titanium composites, resorbable PDS and PLLA/PGA sheets, patient-specific titanium. Biologics enter only as autologous bone (calvarial, iliac, maxillary wall) or as cartilage; no bone graft substitute or growth factor has a labeled or evidence-based role on the orbital floor. A 2026 meta-analysis found no functional advantage of autologous bone over alloplastic implants and more donor morbidity.
autograft_standard: Autologous calvarial bone was the historical gold standard and still used in children and in contaminated or large defects; it resorbs unpredictably and adds a donor site, which is why alloplasts dominate.
volume_note: Nationwide Emergency Department Sample: an estimated 350,379 US ED visits with a primary diagnosis of orbital floor fracture over 2006 to 2017, incidence rising from 7.7 to 11.3 per 100,000 (about 37,000 per year by 2017), 14 percent admitted, assault 43 percent and falls 26 percent (PMID 32659309). Sports-related orbital fractures: national estimate 49,765 over 2014 to 2023 in NEISS (PMID 40550362).
hardware_note: Preformed and patient-specific orbital plates and meshes (Stryker, DePuy Synthes MatrixORBITAL, KLS Martin, Zimmer Biomet, OsteoMed/Acumed), porous polyethylene (Stryker Medpor), resorbable sheets (Synthes PDS, KLS Martin Resorb-x, Stryker Delta, Biomet LactoSorb).

name: Zygomaticomaxillary complex and Le Fort midface fractures

classifications.name: Le Fort I to III
classifications.summary: Le Fort I: horizontal maxillary fracture above the tooth roots separating the palate from the midface. Le Fort II: pyramidal fracture through the nasal bones, medial orbital walls and zygomaticomaxillary buttresses. Le Fort III: craniofacial disjunction through the zygomatic arches, lateral and medial orbital walls and nasofrontal junction. Real injuries are usually mixed and asymmetric.

classifications.name: Zygomaticomaxillary complex (ZMC, tetrapod)
classifications.summary: Fracture through the zygomaticofrontal suture, infraorbital rim and orbital floor, zygomaticomaxillary buttress and zygomatic arch; classified as non-displaced, displaced without comminution, or comminuted; fixation at one to four points.

classifications.name: Midface buttresses
classifications.summary: Vertical nasomaxillary, zygomaticomaxillary and pterygomaxillary buttresses and horizontal frontal bar, infraorbital rims and palate; comminution or loss of a buttress is the indication for a bone graft.

why_biologic: Rarely. These are plate-and-screw fractures. Bone graft is used only to bridge a comminuted or missing buttress or to restore orbital volume, and the graft is almost always autologous calvarial bone. No bone graft substitute carries a midface fracture indication, and no comparative evidence exists for substitutes in acute midface trauma. Calcium phosphate cements and bioactive glass are used off the shelf for secondary contour of the malar and frontal region (Norian CRS, Mimix and HydroSet are labeled for augmentation or restoration of bony contour of the craniofacial skeleton).
autograft_standard: Split calvarial bone for buttress and orbital reconstruction; rib and iliac crest less often. Morbidity is a second scalp incision and rare dural exposure.
volume_note: No US annual count specific to ZMC or Le Fort fractures found. NTDB 2010 to 2019: 155,136 pediatric craniofacial fracture admissions, of which midface 21 percent and orbital floor 13.7 percent (PMID 39042070); NTDB 2016 included 14,447 adult patients with facial fractures in one comparison (PMID 31559862).
hardware_note: Midface plating systems (Stryker, DePuy Synthes MatrixMIDFACE, KLS Martin, Zimmer Biomet, OsteoMed/Acumed) and resorbable fixation for children.

name: Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF), single and multilevel
why_biologic: The interbody space is filled with a structural spacer (cortical ring allograft, PEEK or titanium cage; PEEK and titanium are not biologics) plus a graft material whose job is to bridge the endplates. Biologics here are osteoconductive fillers packed inside the ring or cage, cellular allografts, or the one PMA-approved osteoconductive/peptide composite (i-FACTOR). rhBMP-2 is not approved in the cervical spine and carries an FDA warning.
autograft_standard: Local autograft (vertebral osteophyte and endplate shavings) packed into the spacer, or historically tricortical iliac crest; iliac crest harvest adds donor-site pain, a second incision and limited volume, so most US ACDFs now use allograft ring plus a filler rather than iliac crest.
volume_note: Primary NIS analysis (Saifi 2018, Spine J, PMID 29128581): 1,059,403 ACDFs and 13,099 CDAs in the US 2006-2013; annual ACDF rose 5.7% from 120,617 (2006) to 127,500 (2013), mean 132,425 per year (range 120,617-147,966); ACDF revision burden 2.3%. NIS 2003-2016 Poisson model projects 153,288 to 173,699 ACDFs per year across 2020-2040 (Neifert 2020, PMID 32416237). Single-level ACDF in hospital-owned ASCs rose from 33,687 (2016) to 73,024 (2021). NIS counts inpatient discharges only, so ASC migration since 2013 is not captured.
nonunion_note: Meta-analysis of 21 studies/2,682 patients: fusion 97.1% for single-level plated ACDF, 94.6% for two-level, 82.5% for three-level (Fraser & Hartl 2007). Pooled pseudarthrosis in prospective plated ACDF series 2.6% overall, 0.9% with autograft vs 4.8% with allograft (Shriver 2015).
challenge: NIS is inpatient-only and weighted; the 2006-2013 counts predate the ASC shift, and the 2020-2040 figures are model projections, not observed volumes.

name: Posterior cervical fusion (lateral mass / pedicle screw constructs, including cervicothoracic)
why_biologic: Posterolateral onlay fusion over decorticated lateral masses and facets; the graft bed is small and the host bone is thin, so surgeons extend local autograft with DBM, cellular allograft or synthetic putty. Off-label rhBMP-2 is used in long posterior cervical constructs and revisions but the FDA cervical warning applies to anterior use; posterior use has its own seroma/ectopic bone concerns.
autograft_standard: Local autograft from laminectomy/facetectomy, often supplemented with iliac crest in long or revision constructs; iliac crest adds donor-site morbidity and operative time.
volume_note: NIS 2003-2016 Poisson model projects 29,620 to 35,335 posterior cervical decompression and fusions per year across 2020-2040, with the largest growth in the 75-84 age group (Neifert 2020, World Neurosurg, PMID 32416237; abstract retrieved 2026-10-22).
nonunion_note: Meta-analysis of 10 studies/1,120 multilevel posterior cervical fusions: pooled fusion 86% (constructs ending at C7) and 90% (crossing the cervicothoracic junction); revision 17% vs 7%, not statistically different (Coban 2022).
challenge: No biologic has a posterior-cervical-specific pivotal trial; evidence for any product here is extrapolated from lumbar posterolateral data. The volume figure is a projection from inpatient NIS data.

name: Anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF), stand-alone or with posterior fixation
why_biologic: Large interbody cage packed with graft under compressive load; this is the original on-label Infuse indication (LT-Cage, 2002) and the approach with the best fusion biology, so biologics are used as full autograft replacements inside the cage. rhBMP-2 in ALIF carries a signal for retrograde ejaculation and urogenital events (Fu 2013; Carragee 2011).
autograft_standard: Iliac crest (the Burkus 2002 control) or local bone; in that trial 32% of ICBG patients reported graft-site discomfort at 24 months.
volume_note: Included in NIS elective lumbar fusion totals; no public ALIF-specific annual count found.
nonunion_note: Pooled pseudarthrosis 8.17% across 14 studies/917 patients (2013-2024): 8.95% stand-alone vs 6.76% with posterior fixation, not significant, but stand-alone had RR 6.8 for reoperation for symptomatic pseudarthrosis (Riechelmann 2026). Burkus 2002 pivotal: 94.5% (rhBMP-2) vs 88.7% (ICBG) fusion at 24 months.

name: Intradiscal injection for chronic low back pain due to degenerative disc disease (non-surgical)

classifications.name: Modified Pfirrmann grade
classifications.summary: MRI grading of disc degeneration 1-8; trials of intradiscal biologics typically enroll grades 3-6 (moderate) at a single lumbar level

why_biologic: Allogeneic cells, disc-tissue allograft or autologous concentrates are injected into the nucleus pulposus to reduce discogenic pain and, in theory, slow degeneration; the goal is a non-opioid, non-surgical option between conservative care and fusion.
autograft_standard: No autograft standard exists; comparators are saline/sham injection, conservative care, or fusion/disc replacement surgery. No intradiscal biologic is FDA-licensed.
volume_note: No public procedure-volume source; trials cite chronic low back pain as affecting hundreds of millions worldwide (Spine J 2025, PMID 40174800).

name: Lateral lumbar interbody fusion (LLIF / XLIF / OLIF)
why_biologic: Wide-footprint cage packed with graft; no local bone is generated by the approach, so nearly every lateral fusion uses an allograft, DBM, cellular allograft, synthetic or rhBMP-2 in the cage. Infuse is on-label for OLIF25 (Clydesdale, Pivox; L2-L5) and OLIF51 (Perimeter, Divergence-L; L5-S1) at a single level, and PearlMatrix added single-level OLIF and LLIF in January 2026.
autograft_standard: No local autograft is available from a lateral approach; iliac crest or a separate posterior harvest would be needed, which defeats the minimally invasive intent, so biologics are the de facto standard here.
volume_note: Included in NIS elective lumbar fusion totals; no public lateral-specific annual count found.
nonunion_note: Meta-analysis of 19 XLIF studies/1,409 patients: 12-month fusion rates ranged 85.0% to 93.3% (reported as a range, not a single pooled estimate), transient neurologic events 2.2%, nerve root injury 1.0% (Palacios 2024, PMID 38398273). Stand-alone vs instrumented LLIF meta-analysis (13 studies/1,090 patients): stand-alone fusion RR 0.92 (95% CI 0.87-0.98) with higher subsidence (RR 1.68) and reoperation (RR 2.12) (Yang 2021, PMID 34509241); a 2025 meta-analysis of 12 cohorts/781 patients reached the same direction (Kou 2025, PMID 39948572). Systematic review of MIS lateral surgery (237 articles) did not pool a fusion rate (Lehmen 2015). Product-specific sources: NuVasive-sponsored Osteocel Plus XLIF cohort (n=104, NCT00948532) and PearlMatrix/Infuse labels.
challenge: Lateral fusion evidence is a range (85-93% at 12 months) from single-arm series pooled in a 2024 meta-analysis; there is no independent pooled nonunion estimate for lateral fusion with any specific graft.

name: Posterolateral lumbar fusion (PLF), instrumented
why_biologic: The intertransverse gutter is a large, poorly vascularized onlay bed with no compressive loading, so graft volume and osteoinductive signal both matter. Biologics are used as extenders of local bone (DBM, ceramics, bioactive glass, cellular allograft) or as full substitutes (rhBMP-2 off-label; MagnetOs and some ceramics are 510(k)-cleared as standalone posterolateral fillers). This is the application where most 510(k) bone void filler labels say 'autograft extender in the posterolateral spine'.
autograft_standard: Iliac crest bone graft (ICBG) plus local decompression bone; in the Dimar 2009 pivotal control arm 60% of ICBG patients still reported donor-site pain at 24 months, and ICBG fused only 89% at 24 months.
volume_note: Elective lumbar fusion volume (all approaches) rose 62.3% from 122,679 (2004) to 199,140 (2015) in the NIS; spondylolisthesis and scoliosis were the fastest-growing indications (Martin 2019).
nonunion_note: ICBG control arms in RCTs: 89% fusion at 24 months (Dimar 2009, n=463); side-by-side Grafton vs ICBG 52% vs 54% per-side fusion at 24 months by blinded plain radiograph (Cammisa 2004, n=120); autograft side fused only 47% by CT at 1 year in the MagnetOs intra-patient RCT (Stempels 2024). Nonunion rates therefore range from about 10% to over 40% depending on imaging and definition.

name: Transforaminal / posterior lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF, PLIF, MIS-TLIF)
why_biologic: The cage is packed with graft to bridge the endplates under compression; local bone from the decompression is often insufficient for cage plus posterolateral gutters, so extenders and substitutes are used inside the cage. Until 2025 no biologic carried a TLIF indication; PearlMatrix (June 2025) and Infuse (February 2026) now do, which changes the on-label conversation for the single largest lumbar fusion category.
autograft_standard: Local autograft from the facetectomy and laminectomy; iliac crest is rarely harvested for TLIF today. Local bone alone had the lowest pooled fusion rate (91.8%) in a MIS-TLIF meta-analysis, and only 58.5% fused by strict CT criteria at 24 months in the ASPIRE control arm.
volume_note: Included in the 199,140 elective lumbar fusions (2015, NIS; Martin 2019); interbody approaches are the majority of these but the NIS does not separate TLIF from PLIF.
nonunion_note: MIS-TLIF meta-analysis of 40 series/1,533 patients: fusion 91.8% (local bone alone) to 99.1% (local bone + extender + rhBMP-2); 96.6% all rhBMP-2 series vs 92.5% non-rhBMP-2 (Parajon 2017). ASPIRE RCT control arm (local autograft, PEEK cage, pedicle screws): fusion 58.5% at 24 months by CT with about 60% high-risk patients (Harrop 2025).

name: Minimally invasive sacroiliac joint fusion
why_biologic: Two segments. (1) Lateral/posterolateral transfixing implants (SI-BONE iFuse, iFuse-3D, iFuse TORQ, iFuse Bedrock Granite; Globus SI-LOK/SI-LOK SELECT; Orthofix FIREBIRD SI; Medtronic Rialto, K251395 2025; Camber Siconus; Spinal Simplicity Liberty-SI; Aurora SiLO TFX, K221047; CornerLoc TransLoc 3D, K232878; Tenon Catamaran; Tenon SImmetry+) are 510(k) titanium devices whose fusion claim rests on porous/coated surfaces and, in the fenestrated screws, bone that the implant self-harvests through its flutes (iFuse-3D 'fenestrated design to self-harvest bone'; FIREBIRD 'radial fenestrations allow self-harvesting of autograft'; SI-LOK 'optional graft slot'; Rialto IFU 'autograft and/or allograft may be placed in conjunction'). The INSITE, iMIA and SALLY trials of iFuse used no added graft. None of these vendors' product pages names a cellular allograft or DBM for the SI joint, so biologic use with transfixing screws is surgeon-discretionary and unbranded. (2) Posterior intra-articular 'fusion' implants ARE the biologic: machined structural cortical allograft dowels or spacers placed into the decorticated joint, regulated as 361 HCT/Ps (homologous use) rather than cleared devices. Products: PainTEQ LinQ (and the cortical-piercing TRAQ), SI-BONE iFuse INTRA V/INTRA X (supplied by an undisclosed third-party tissue bank), Aurora Spine SiLO, CornerLoc grafts (cortical graft plus a DBM sponge), Omnia Medical PsiF allograft, Vyrsa Pro (Vyrsa -> Nevro 2023 -> Globus 2025). Several are packed with DBM in a graft window at the surgeon's discretion. Titanium posterior 'in-line' implants (Camber SI, Spinal Simplicity Patriot-SI, CornerLoc TransLoc 3D posterior, Omnia PsiF DNA K-cleared May 2025, SI-BONE iFuse INTRA Ti) are moving the posterior approach back to 510(k) metal that must be paired with, or itself pierces, cortical bone.
autograft_standard: No iliac crest is harvested in MIS SI fusion. For transfixing screws the 'autograft' is local bone self-harvested by the fenestrated implant; for posterior allograft systems the graft is the implant itself (structural cortical allograft, optionally with DBM in the window). Open SI arthrodesis historically used iliac crest from the adjacent ilium.
volume_note: Medicare fee-for-service: 33,963 SI joint fusions 2010-2020, rising from 318 (2010) to 7,794 (2020); 68.5% MIS (CPT 27279) since 2015 (Federico 2023). SI-BONE reports supporting 'a total of over 140,000 procedures' since 2009 and about 1,640 US physicians performing a procedure in Q4 2025; FY2025 worldwide revenue $200.9M (+20.2%), US $191.1M, 2026 guidance $228.5-232.5M (8-K exhibit 99.1, Feb 23 2026).
nonunion_note: INSITE RCT (n=148, SI-BONE sponsored): 6-month success 81.4% surgical vs 26.1% nonsurgical; 3 revisions in 102 fusions at 24 months. Pooled figures: meta-analysis of 48 studies found pooled fusion rates numerically similar across lateral, posterior and posterolateral approaches, with pooled revision 2.4% lateral vs 0.6% posterior and complications 9.2% vs 1% (Xu 2025, PMID 39917851); meta-analysis of 2 RCTs and 9 prospective cohorts (1,181 fusions, mean 27.8 months) found implant-related reoperation 3% (95% CI 2-4%) (Baur 2026, PMID 42023816); a 57-cohort review (2,851 patients) notes independent radiographic fusion evidence exists only for lateral transiliac devices (Whang 2023, SI-BONE-authored, PMID 37798076). No independent nonunion rate for graft-packed posterior SI systems was found.
challenge: The cumulative SI-BONE count (over 140,000 since 2009, replacing the earlier 'nearly 150,000' wording) is a company figure from its 8-K. Which graft products are packed in posterior SI systems, and by whom, was still not verified; pooled 'fusion' for posterior interpositional systems rests on company-affiliated reviews.
coverage_note: CPT: 27279 (lateral/transfixing, since 2015; device-intensive in ASC, 2026 CMS unadjusted ASC $14,518, HOPD APC 5116 $17,914) and 27278 (posterior intra-articular, no transfixation; Category I since 1 Jan 2024 replacing Category III 0775T, which existed 2022-2023; 2026 ASC $15,048, same APC 5116). For 2026 the AMA revised both descriptors: 27279 = transarticular and/or intra-articular device(s) piercing the ilium/sacrum cortices, 27278 = intra-articular device(s) without cortical piercing, so cortical-piercing posterior products (PainTEQ TRAQ, SI-BONE INTRA Ti) bill 27279 and hybrids (posterior in-line plus transfixing screw) bill 27279. Medicare physician fee 2026: 27279 $762; 27278 $441 facility / $13,834 office-based lab (SI-BONE 10-K). Inpatient (rare): ICD-10-PCS 0SG734Z/0SG834Z group to FY2026 MS-DRG 450/451 Single Level Spinal Fusion Except Cervical with/without MCC ($38,782 / $23,507 unadjusted; SI-BONE facility guide Feb 2026). Device C-codes C1889/C1776 are packaged (no separate payment). Medicare coverage: CGS (L39802, KY/OH), Noridian (L39810/L39812, JE/JF; JF retired 23 Oct 2025 into the JE policy) and Palmetto (L39797, JJ/JM) finalized LCDs effective 17 Apr 2025 (Noridian 16 Feb 2025) stating that MI arthrodesis of the SIJ 'WITHOUT placement of a transfixation device is NOT considered medically reasonable and necessary', i.e. 27278/posterior allograft is non-covered in those jurisdictions; the Noridian evidence review quotes ISASS that posterior MI SIJF is 'unproven and not recommended'. SI-BONE's 10-K says these LCDs 'precluding coverage for CPT 27278' reduced demand for INTRA X. NGS/Wellpoint (L36406, revised 1 Apr 2026) and WPS (L36000, rev. 27 Jun 2024) still describe the covered procedure as 'percutaneous insertion of a metallic device across the SIJ' without naming 27278; Novitas and First Coast have no SI fusion LCD that this pass could find. ACR, ASPN and NANS objected to the three 2025 LCDs; the LCDs stand as of Oct 2026. iFuse Bedrock Granite received hospital-outpatient/ASC transitional pass-through from 1 Jan 2025 and iFuse TORQ TNT an NTAP (hardware, not biologics).

name: Adult spinal deformity / long-segment fusion to the sacrum or pelvis
why_biologic: Long constructs (often 8-12 levels) with osteotomies, older patients and fusion to S1/pelvis have the highest pseudarthrosis rates in spine surgery and need more graft than any patient can donate. rhBMP-2 is used off-label in roughly three quarters of ISSG deformity cases at a mean 23.6 mg per patient, usually with allograft or ceramic extenders, and revision for pseudarthrosis was 8.6% with BMP vs 17% without (Jain 2020).
autograft_standard: Local bone from osteotomies plus iliac crest; iliac crest is often inadequate in volume for 10+ levels, is compromised by pelvic fixation, and in the Maeda 2009 series the ICBG group had a 28.1% pseudarthrosis rate vs 4.3% with rhBMP-2.
volume_note: NIS elective lumbar fusions coded for degenerative scoliosis grew 186.6% (+16,129 operations) from 2004 to 2015, implying roughly 24,800 such fusions in 2015 (derived from Martin 2019).
nonunion_note: Pseudarthrosis 24% in 144 long fusions to the sacrum (Kim 2006, Spine) and 17% in 232 long adult deformity fusions (Kim 2006, JBJS); 11% revision for symptomatic pseudarthrosis in 367 ISSG patients with 5+ levels (Jain 2020).

name: Vertebral compression fracture: vertebral augmentation with resorbable or bioactive fill (biologic/resorbable materials only)

classifications.name: Genant semiquantitative grading (1993)
classifications.summary: Visual grading of vertebral height loss on lateral radiographs: grade 0 normal; grade 1 mild (about 20-25% height reduction); grade 2 moderate (about 25-40%); grade 3 severe (more than 40%); each with wedge, biconcave or crush morphology. Thresholds are the commonly cited values; the original paper is PMID 8237484.

classifications.name: AO Spine-DGOU osteoporotic fracture (OF) classification (Schnake 2018)
classifications.summary: OF1 no deformation, edema on MRI only; OF2 deformation of one endplate with no or minor (<1/5) posterior wall involvement; OF3 deformation with distinct (>1/5) posterior wall involvement; OF4 loss of vertebral frame integrity, body collapse or pincer fracture; OF5 injuries with distraction or rotation. Interobserver kappa 0.63.

why_biologic: Standard augmentation uses PMMA, which is not a biologic and does not remodel; resorbable calcium phosphate cements (e.g., KyphOs FS) and the bioactive glass-ceramic composite Cortoss were developed to osseointegrate or better match bone stiffness. The RCT evidence shows CPC can fail mechanically in burst-type fractures, so resorbable fill is a niche, not the standard.
autograft_standard: No autograft role; the comparator is PMMA vertebroplasty/kyphoplasty, or non-operative bracing.
volume_note: Medicare: 77,276 augmentation claims at the 2008 peak; 2015 counts were 13,478 vertebroplasties and 57,646 kyphoplasties (Rabei 2019). A separate 2012-2017 physician-claims analysis found kyphoplasty fell to 21,681 and vertebroplasty to 2,987 by 2017 (Lopez 2020); the two papers use different Medicare files so they are not comparable.
nonunion_note: Not a fusion; failure modes are cement failure/loss of correction and adjacent fracture. CPC kyphoplasty RCT (n=56): 9 radiographic losses of correction in the CPC arm vs 0 with PMMA (Blattert 2009). Cortoss vs PMMA RCT (n=256): noninferior, 4.3% serious device-related events in both arms, subsequent fractures 27.8% vs 31.9% (Bae 2012; Gilula 2012).

name: Congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia (CPT), surgical reconstruction

classifications.name: Paley classification of CPT
classifications.summary: Types 1-4 by whether the tibia is intact or fractured and whether the fracture is mobile; Novadip's Phase 3 enrolls non-healing Paley type 3 or 4 diaphyseal fractures

why_biologic: CPT (often with NF1) is a rare pediatric nonunion in which iliac crest bone graft plus intramedullary rodding frequently fails, leading to repeated surgery and sometimes amputation; an osteogenic autologous graft is intended to achieve union where ICBG does not.
autograft_standard: Iliac crest bone graft with intramedullary rod fixation is the comparator in NCT07112443; limited volume in small children and high refracture/nonunion rates are the downside.
volume_note: Rare disease; FDA granted orphan and rare pediatric disease designations (Novadip press release, Dec 23, 2020). No US volume figure located.

name: Pilon (tibial plafond) fracture: staged ORIF with metaphyseal void fill

classifications.name: Rüedi-Allgöwer
classifications.summary: Type I articular fracture without significant displacement; type II displaced articular surface without comminution; type III comminuted, impacted articular surface with metaphyseal defect.

classifications.name: AO/OTA 43
classifications.summary: 43-A extra-articular, 43-B partial articular, 43-C complete articular (C3 comminuted). Metaphyseal impaction in 43-C leaves a void after articular reduction.

why_biologic: Impacted metaphyseal bone leaves a cavity after reduction of the plafond; a void filler supports the articular segment. Because the soft-tissue envelope is fragile and infection risk high (pooled SSI 17%), surgeons favor fillers that do not need a second incision, and an antibiotic-eluting filler is being studied for open pilons.
autograft_standard: Autograft (ICBG or local) for metaphyseal defects when needed; staged protocol (spanning external fixation, then ORIF when soft tissue allows) is the main driver of outcomes. No RCT of void fillers specific to pilon was found.
volume_note: No public US volume found; pilon fractures are a small fraction of tibial fractures. Systematic reviews report nonunion 0.6% (MIPO series) to about 10% malunion/nonunion in staged treatment of C3 fractures.

name: Patella fracture: fixation with occasional graft of comminuted or periprosthetic defects

classifications.name: AO/OTA 34
classifications.summary: 34-A extra-articular (avulsion), 34-B partial articular (vertical), 34-C complete articular (C1 transverse, C2 transverse with second fragment, C3 comminuted); 34-C3 is the most common pattern (25%).

why_biologic: Biologics have almost no role in primary patella fixation; the only niche is bone loss in comminuted or periprosthetic patellar fractures and patellar nonunion, where small-volume void fillers or DBM are used ad hoc. Included so the knee section is complete and to document that no product carries patella-specific evidence.
autograft_standard: Tension-band or suture-anchor fixation without graft; partial patellectomy for an unreconstructable pole. Periprosthetic patellar fracture ORIF with wiring has nonunion/failure rates reported as high as 90%.
volume_note: Danish incidence 13.1 per 100,000 per year (756 fractures over 10 years). No US count found.

name: Medial opening-wedge high tibial osteotomy: gap fill

classifications.name: Osteotomy gap size
classifications.summary: Gaps under 10 mm are usually left unfilled with a locking plate; gaps over 10 mm (large corrections) are where wedges or fillers are used. Lateral hinge fracture (Takeuchi I-III) raises nonunion risk.

why_biologic: The opening wedge creates a defect that must consolidate under a locking plate; fillers (beta-TCP or HA/TCP wedges, allograft wedges, calcium phosphate cement) are structural extenders meant to reduce loss of correction and nonunion for large gaps. Evidence says filler choice does not change outcomes for gaps under 10 mm.
autograft_standard: Iliac crest autograft was the historical gap filler; an RCT (n=46) found iliac allograft equivalent with no nonunions in either arm, and 52% of autograft patients had worse donor-site pain than osteotomy pain.
volume_note: No US count found; HTO volume in the US is small relative to arthroplasty. A 2026 systematic review of 1,640 knees found 36% allograft, 30% no filler, 22% synthetic, 12% autograft.

name: Tibial plateau fracture: ORIF with subchondral void fill

classifications.name: Schatzker I-VI
classifications.summary: I lateral split; II lateral split-depression; III pure lateral depression; IV medial plateau; V bicondylar; VI bicondylar with metaphyseal-diaphyseal dissociation. Depression patterns (II, III, and many V/VI) leave a subchondral metaphyseal void after elevation.

classifications.name: AO/OTA 41-B/41-C
classifications.summary: 41-B partial articular (B2 pure depression, B3 split-depression); 41-C complete articular (bicondylar). CERTiFy and most void-filler RCTs enrolled 41-B2/B3.

why_biologic: After the depressed articular segment is elevated, the metaphyseal cavity must be filled so the joint surface does not re-subside; the filler is a structural, osteoconductive void fill (calcium phosphate cement, calcium sulfate/HA composite, beta-TCP) rather than an osteoinductive agent. This is the single largest trauma use of synthetic bone void fillers.
autograft_standard: Autologous iliac crest cancellous graft is the historical standard but is weak in compression, adds donor-site pain (reported in all 38 autograft patients in one RCT) and blood loss; RCTs show calcium phosphate cement reduces subsidence versus autograft and CERAMENT BVF is noninferior.
volume_note: No US-specific annual count found in public sources. Danish population data give tibial plateau fractures about 10 per 100,000 per year; US tibial fracture volumes are reported only in aggregate. Cochrane 2024 pooled 15 RCTs (948 patients), six of them void-filler trials.

name: Aseptic tibial nonunion: revision fixation with biologic augmentation

classifications.name: Weber-Cech / FDA nonunion definition
classifications.summary: Hypertrophic (vascular, needs stability), oligotrophic, and atrophic (avascular, needs biology). FDA-style definition used in trials: fracture at least 9 months old with no radiographic progression for 3 months.

why_biologic: Atrophic and oligotrophic nonunions need biological stimulus as well as mechanical stability; the biologic supplies osteoinduction (rhBMP-7 historically, rhBMP-2 off-label), osteogenic cells (BMAC, percutaneous marrow injection) or an osteoconductive scaffold (DBM, ceramics) in the diamond-concept framework.
autograft_standard: Exchange reamed nailing for hypertrophic shaft nonunion; autogenous cancellous graft (ICBG or RIA) plus revision fixation for atrophic nonunion. ICBG complication rate 19.4% versus 6% for RIA in a 6,682-patient systematic review.
volume_note: US claims analysis of 309,330 fractures: overall nonunion 4.9%, with tibia plus fibula among the three highest-risk sites; open fracture OR 1.66 and operative treatment OR 1.78 for nonunion.

name: Closed tibial shaft fracture: reamed IM nail (biologics not indicated)

classifications.name: AO/OTA 42
classifications.summary: 42-A simple, 42-B wedge, 42-C multifragmentary; closed soft-tissue injury graded by Tscherne (C0-C3).

why_biologic: Included as a negative control application: two sponsored RCTs (rhBMP-2/calcium phosphate matrix in closed fractures, n=369; rhBMP-2/ACS with reamed nails in open fractures, n=277) showed no acceleration of healing, and the LIPUS TRUST trial (n=501) was negative. No biologic has an on-label indication here and routine use is not supported.
autograft_standard: Reamed, locked IM nailing alone; SPRINT showed a possible benefit of reaming for closed fractures. Grafting is reserved for established delayed union or nonunion.
volume_note: Tibial shaft fractures are the most common long-bone fracture; Danish incidence 16.9 per 100,000 per year. No US count found.

name: Infected tibial nonunion / fracture-related infection: debridement, dead-space fill, staged reconstruction

classifications.name: Cierny-Mader
classifications.summary: Anatomic type I medullary, II superficial, III localized, IV diffuse; host class A healthy, B compromised (local or systemic), C treatment worse than disease. Most tibial FRI series are type III-IV in B hosts.

why_biologic: After radical debridement the dead space must be filled to prevent hematoma and reinfection; antibiotic-eluting calcium sulfate or calcium sulfate/hydroxyapatite composites deliver local antibiotic at concentrations far above MIC while resorbing, allowing single-stage treatment instead of PMMA beads plus a second surgery.
autograft_standard: Historical standard is two-stage: debridement with PMMA antibiotic beads or an antibiotic spacer, systemic antibiotics, then autograft (ICBG, RIA) or bone transport once infection is controlled; union rates 73-100% across series.
volume_note: No US count found. Tibia is the most common osteomyelitis site in multinational series (116-patient S53P4 registry). METRC is running a 250-patient RCT of oral versus IV antibiotics for infected nonunion after fixation (NCT05699174).

name: Open tibial shaft fracture: IM nail with adjunct biologic

classifications.name: Gustilo-Anderson
classifications.summary: I wound under 1 cm, clean; II wound 1-10 cm without extensive soft-tissue damage; IIIA extensive soft-tissue damage but adequate coverage; IIIB periosteal stripping requiring flap coverage; IIIC arterial injury requiring repair. BESTT and FORTIFY enrolled Gustilo II-IIIB.

classifications.name: AO/OTA 42
classifications.summary: 42-A simple, 42-B wedge, 42-C multifragmentary diaphyseal tibia.

why_biologic: Open tibial shaft fractures have the highest infection and nonunion rates of any common long-bone injury; the biologic is used at definitive closure either as an osteoinductive adjunct to reduce secondary intervention (rhBMP-2, the only on-label BMP trauma indication) or, since 2024, as an antibiotic-eluting void filler to fill bone loss and lower infection (CERAMENT G).
autograft_standard: Standard of care is reamed or unreamed IM nailing with staged autograft (ICBG or RIA) only if a defect or delayed union declares itself; acute bone grafting of an open wound is avoided because of infection risk, which is the gap biologics try to fill.
volume_note: US-specific incidence not found. Swedish registry: 12% of tibial shaft fractures are open, about 2.3 per 100,000 person-years; Dutch 2018-2019 hospital data: 34% of admitted tibial fractures coded open. Overall tibial shaft incidence about 16.9 per 100,000 per year (Danish data).

name: Segmental tibial bone defect: induced membrane (Masquelet) versus bone transport

classifications.name: Defect size / Paley
classifications.summary: Critical-size diaphyseal loss is commonly taken as more than 2-2.5 cm or more than 50% circumference; outcomes stratified under and over 7 cm (infection risk rises above 7 cm after induced membrane). Paley classifies nonunion-defect by mobility and bone loss.

why_biologic: In the two-stage induced membrane technique the PMMA spacer creates a vascularized membrane and the second stage is filled with autograft, which is the biologic step; graft volume limits drive the use of RIA, allograft chips, DBM, ceramics and, off-label, rhBMP-2 as extenders. Bone transport (Ilizarov or magnetic intramedullary) is the non-biologic alternative that avoids graft altogether.
autograft_standard: Stage-two autograft: RIA from the femur (large volume) or ICBG, often mixed with allograft or synthetic extender. Pooled tibial union after Masquelet 84% (643 tibiae) versus 94.6% for distraction osteogenesis in infected tibial defects (not significant).
volume_note: No public US volume. Masquelet series pool a few hundred tibiae worldwide; US military trauma drove much of the literature.
